newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares surge on foreign interest..
newsitem.headline: Danish shares surge on foreign interest..

text.p: Foreign buying interest pushed Danish share prices higher on Thursday and the upward trend was expected to continue on Friday, albeit with morning trade quiet ahead of the KFX November future's expiry.
"There is a positive undertone to the market and the expectation is that prices will rise further, although turnover will be lower," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index rose 0.94 point to 128.70 in overall bourse turnover of 537 million crowns. The KFX November future rose 1.0 point to 129. The December future rose 0.90 point to 129.30, with 1,199 contracts, each of 100,000 crowns, traded.

SAS, in need of extensive cost-cutting to reverse declining profitability, was the most-traded paper on Thursday with 95,000 shares trading hands, although the price moved relatively little, down 0.50 to 71 crowns. The share was downgraded by Den Danske Bank on Tuesday.
The bank itself moved in the opposite direction on Thursday, up four crowns to 435 crowns.

Novo Nordisk, which posted better-than-expected third quarter results on Wednesday, rose eight crowns to 1,000 crowns, with about 63,000 shares traded. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969656
